name: A Remote Signed-Clause Pivot Can Remove a Forbidden pc-Minor
statement: For every $j\ge0$ there are two-connected ample families $X_j,Y_j\subseteq Q_{24+2j}$ with $X_j$ pc-minimal outside dismantlable ampleness and $Y_j$ dismantlable ample. Every proper pc-minor of either is dismantlable ample. They have the same shadow, differ in one four-support clause by antipodal signs, agree through Hamming radius $j+4$ about zero, and first differ at radius $j+5$. Their common order is $(581\cdot3^j+575)/2$ and their VC dimension is $3+j$. Thus the marked local ball and complete shadow do not determine forbidden-minor membership, even among two-connected ample classes whose proper minors all peel.
proof: Glue each rooted pair member at zero to a fresh copy of the fixed rooted factor. The negative wedge is a cut-vertex forbidden pc-minor, while the positive wedge peels blockwise. Complete the same cross-block square in both families. The square-completed rooted-block theorem makes the negative side a two-connected forbidden pc-minor; the new degree-two corner and the block orders peel the positive side. The common addition preserves the unique changed clause and the distance profile. Product-layer connectivity and the new square tip prove two-connectivity on the positive side.
